A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FastMCTS work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including relocated algorithms and renumbered appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original sampling-efficiency experiments, downstream supervised fine-tuning and Branch-DPO results, difficulty analyses and component ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original few-shot-ablation results, difficulty-distribution measurements and training comparisons using two additional base models.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 and the Adaptive Stay, Dynamic Exploration, simulation retention, few-shot prompting and SFT/Branch-DPO procedures remain unchanged. The expanded node and verifier descriptions disclose implementation details without establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: The English and Chinese math training corpora and evaluation tasks are retained. The added model comparisons use existing benchmarks. Newly documented filtering rules explain the existing data selection rather than establish changed dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix I/Table 7 substantially expands the reported comparator set with GPT-4o, NuminaMath-CoT-7B, NuminaMath-TIR-7B, OpenMath2-Llama3.1-8B and rStarMath Policy 7B. These comparisons are absent from v1; the existing rejection-sampling and vanilla-MCTS comparisons remain.

E3.justification: Appendix H adds Llama-3.2-3B and Qwen2.5-3B training configurations using the existing English math setup and three-epoch checkpoint selection. v2 also introduces entropy as an analysis metric and a no-few-shot control. The original experiments' stated budgets and evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing difficulty and component analyses receive focused extensions: entropy measurements in Table 4, a few-shot-removal ablation in Table 5, and tests of robustness to base-model family and size in Appendix H. The original analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions describe ablations as averaged over multiple runs without specifying run counts, seeds or statistical uncertainty. v2's newly disclosed three-pass judge consensus concerns data verification, not uncertainty estimation for the reported experimental scores.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the original plotted results are unchanged, but Tables 4–7 add substantial results. Table 6 reports FastMCTS versus RS averages of 26.7 versus 25.4 for Llama-3.2-3B and 47.4 versus 45.3 for Qwen2.5-3B. Table 5 adds 60.7% solving rate and 7.37 correct paths without few-shot examples. Table 7 adds comparator scores while reusing existing FastMCTS results.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 and the assumptions underlying Branch-DPO construction remain unchanged. The new Appendix A illustrates the existing step-to-node mapping with a worked math example; it introduces no substantive theoretical definition, assumption or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims of efficient, difficulty-balanced synthesis and improved downstream training. Both abstracts retain the claims of over 30% more correct reasoning paths and a 3.9% performance advantage.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the limitation of testing only Qwen2.5-7B with an explicit math-domain-only limitation and interprets the additional model tests as evidence of broader applicability. Appendix I adds discussion of competitive performance and possible improvements from better data curation. Generator and prefix-repetition limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility information: step-format examples, few-shot subject coverage, Qwen2.5-32B filtering with five samples per question, exclusion and deduplication rules, and the verifier prompt, 32-token output limit and consensus procedure. It also adds a repository link, although code release is still described as forthcoming. Existing sampling and training hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: The related-work section and reference list are unchanged in substance. Appendix I adds a limited positioning discussion comparing FastMCTS with recent general and math-specialized models, emphasizing competitive performance and data-curation constraints.

P1.justification: The main section order and most original prose remain intact. v2 makes limited wording, affiliation and numbering corrections, adds explanatory passages and acknowledgments, and expands and renumbers the appendices.

P2.justification: The presentation expands substantially through three new empirical tables, the full-width verifier-prompt Figure 5 and a boxed node-by-node example. The ablation table gains a row and moves, and Figure 4 is relocated. Existing plots and algorithm displays are retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's single-base-model training tests and terse filtering/verifier descriptions, v2 provides useful cross-model checks, a few-shot ablation and concrete implementation details. These improve reproducibility and support for the existing claims. The gain is bounded by unchanged uncertainty reporting and insufficiently documented common conditions for the new recent-work comparison in Table 7.
